title: Quantum-mechanical wave functions in singular potentials: linear and nonlinear states
abstract: It is known that the attractive singular inverse-square potential gives rise to the critical quantum collapse in the framework of the three-dimensional (3D) linear Schroedinger equation. This article summarizes theoretical results which demonstrate suppression of the collapse, caused by this singular potential, and the creation of the otherwise missing ground state (GS) in a 3D gas of bosonic particles, carrying an electric dipole moment, which are pulled to the central electric charge, with repulsive contact interactions between the particles. In the mean-field approximation, the repulsive interactions are represented by the cubic term in the respective Gross-Pitaevskii (GP) equation. In addition to the GS, excited states with angular momentum are briefly considered too. Another topic considered in the article is 1D and 2D bound states in the linear Schroedinger and GP equations with the repulsive potential, which demonstrates a singularity at r --> infinity. A very recent result is that such a potential, growing faster than the negative harmonic-oscillator potential, produces a full spectrum of counter-intuitive normalizable (localized) bound states. The article puts forward perspectives for further studies of linear and nonlinear bound states existing under the action of the potentials with the singularity at r --> 0 or r --> infinity.
summary: This article theoretically explores quantum wave functions in systems governed by singular potentials, such as the inverse-square potential. It demonstrates that repulsive nonlinear interactions can prevent quantum collapse in 3D bosonic gases. Furthermore, it shows that potentials growing faster than the harmonic oscillator can support a full spectrum of localized bound states, offering insights into trapping mechanisms in quantum matter.
main_problem: The paper investigates the behavior of quantum-mechanical wave functions in the presence of singular potentials, specifically addressing the phenomenon of quantum collapse and the existence of localized bound states.
main_result: The addition of repulsive contact interactions (nonlinear terms) can suppress quantum collapse caused by singular inverse-square potentials, and steep repulsive potentials ($\gamma > 1$) can generate a full spectrum of localized bound states.
method: The analysis relies on solving the linear and nonlinear Schrödinger and Gross-Pitaevskii equations (GPE) in various dimensions (1D, 2D, 3D) using mean-field approximations and asymptotic analysis.
model_or_system: The models include bosonic gases interacting via repulsive contact terms, subjected to singular potentials at $r 	o 0$ (inverse-square potential) and potentials that grow steeply at $r 	o \infty$ (expulsive potentials).
key_observables: Ground state wave functions ($\Psi$), chemical potential ($\mu$), binding energy, and the stability of vortex states.
important_parameters: Singular potential strength ($U_0$), nonlinearity strength ($g$), and the potential steepness parameter ($\gamma$).
main_assumptions: The primary approximations involve the mean-field approximation (MFA) for repulsive interactions, and analyzing the system in the stationary state limit.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate numerical solutions for the radial profile of the wave function ($\chi(r)$) in 3D, and time evolution snapshots showing the stability of quantum droplets.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the problem in three parts: 1) 3D collapse suppression using the GPE; 2) Analysis of 2D/3D vortex states; and 3) Examination of 1D and 2D bound states under potentials singular at $r 	o \infty$.
why_interesting: It provides a comprehensive theoretical framework for understanding how nonlinear interactions and specific potential geometries can stabilize quantum systems against collapse or induce novel localized states, which is crucial for modeling trapped ultracold atoms.
